points.title: 童年时期
points.description: 西尔维娅·普拉斯于1932年10月27日出生于马萨诸塞州波士顿的一个中产阶级家庭。她的父亲奥托·普拉斯是德国移民，波士顿大学生物学教授，于1940年因糖尿病并发症去世，这一事件对普拉斯产生了深远影响。普拉斯从小就展现出非凡的文学天赋，8岁时开始写诗，11岁时在《波士顿旅行者》上发表第一首诗。这段时期她经历了父亲早逝的创伤，同时也培养了强烈的文学抱负和完美主义倾向。
points.descriptionEn: Sylvia Plath was born on October 27, 1932, in Boston, Massachusetts, to a middle-class family. Her father, Otto Plath, was a German immigrant and biology professor at Boston University, who died from complications of diabetes in 1940, an event that profoundly affected Plath. From an early age, Plath showed exceptional literary talent, writing poetry at age 8 and publishing her first poem in the Boston Herald at age 11. During this period, she experienced the trauma of her father's early death while developing strong literary ambitions and perfectionist tendencies.

points.title: 大学教育
points.description: 普拉斯进入史密斯学院学习，这是美国最顶尖的女子学院之一。在校期间，她成绩优异，获得多项奖学金，同时积极参与校园文学活动，担任《史密斯评论》编辑。这一时期她开始创作短篇小说，并获得多个写作奖项。1953年，她经历了一次精神崩溃，尝试自杀未遂，随后接受电休克治疗。这段经历成为她后来作品中的重要主题。1955年，她以优异成绩毕业并获得富布赖特奖学金，准备前往英国剑桥大学深造。
points.descriptionEn: Plath attended Smith College, one of America's top women's colleges. During her studies, she excelled academically, received multiple scholarships, and actively participated in campus literary activities, serving as editor of the Smith Review. During this time, she began writing short stories and won several writing awards. In 1953, she experienced a mental breakdown, attempted suicide, and subsequently received electroshock therapy. This experience became a significant theme in her later work. In 1955, she graduated with highest honors and received a Fulbright scholarship to study at Cambridge University in England.

points.title: 剑桥岁月
points.description: 在剑桥大学，普拉斯成为纽纳姆学院的学生，专攻英语文学。在这里，她遇到了未来的丈夫特德·休斯，一位才华横溢的英国诗人。两人于1956年结婚，这段关系成为普拉斯生活中重要而复杂的一部分。在剑桥期间，普拉斯继续创作诗歌，并开始发展自己独特的诗歌风格，融合了个人痛苦与精湛的技巧。她完成了短篇小说《钟形罩》的初稿，这部作品后来成为她唯一的长篇小说。剑桥时期标志着她从学生向成熟作家的转变，也是她文学风格形成的关键阶段。
points.descriptionEn: At Cambridge University, Plath studied at Newnham College, specializing in English literature. There, she met her future husband, Ted Hughes, a talented British poet. They married in 1956, and this relationship became an important yet complex part of Plath's life. During her time in Cambridge, Plath continued writing poetry and began developing her distinctive poetic style, blending personal pain with technical mastery. She completed the first draft of her later novel 'The Bell Jar.' The Cambridge period marked her transition from student to mature writer and was a crucial phase in the development of her literary style.

points.place: 马萨诸塞州波士顿和英国伦敦
points.title: 婚姻与创作
points.description: 普拉斯与休斯婚后在波士顿和伦敦两地生活。1957-1958年，她在史密斯学院教授英语，但很快辞职专注于写作。1959年，他们回到英国，在德文郡定居。这一时期普拉斯经历了创作高峰，完成了大量诗歌和短篇小说。1960年，她的第一本诗集《巨像及其他诗作》出版。1961年，女儿弗里达出生。然而，婚姻关系逐渐紧张，普拉斯发现丈夫有外遇。1962年，他们分居，普拉斯带着两个孩子搬到伦敦的奇西克，开始了她最具创造力的时期之一，创作了后来收入《爱丽尔》诗集的许多重要作品。
points.descriptionEn: After marriage, Plath and Hughes lived between Boston and London. From 1957-1958, she taught English at Smith College but soon resigned to focus on writing. In 1959, they returned to England and settled in Devon. During this period, Plath experienced a creative peak, producing numerous poems and short stories. In 1960, her first poetry collection 'The Colossus and Other Poems' was published. In 1961, her daughter Frieda was born. However, the marriage became increasingly strained as Plath discovered Hughes's infidelity. In 1962, they separated, and Plath moved with their two children to Chiswick, London, beginning one of her most creative periods, writing many poems that would later be included in her collection 'Ariel.'

points.title: 最后岁月
points.description: 1962年末至1963年初是普拉斯生命中最艰难也最富创造力的时期。她完成了自传体小说《钟形罩》，这部作品以笔名出版，描述了她与抑郁症斗争的经历。1963年1月，小说出版后获得广泛好评。然而，普拉斯的抑郁症日益严重，她开始接受精神治疗。1963年2月，她与休斯离婚。同年3月，她搬到伦敦市中心的塔维斯托克路公寓，继续写作。1963年2月11日，在完成最后一首诗后，普拉斯在公寓内自杀身亡，年仅30岁。她的去世使她成为文学史上最具传奇色彩和悲剧色彩的人物之一，她的作品在她死后才获得广泛认可和赞誉。
points.descriptionEn: Late 1962 to early 1963 was the most difficult yet creatively productive period of Plath's life. She completed her autobiographical novel 'The Bell Jar,' published under a pseudonym, describing her experiences with depression. The novel received widespread acclaim upon its publication in January 1963. However, Plath's depression worsened, and she began psychiatric treatment. In February 1963, she divorced Hughes. That same March, she moved to an apartment in Tavistock Square, central London, continuing to write. On February 11, 1963, after completing her final poem, Plath committed suicide in her apartment at age 30. Her death made her one of the most legendary and tragic figures in literary history, with her works gaining widespread recognition and acclaim only after her death.

appraisal.zh: 普拉斯如今被公认为自白派诗歌的代表人物，其诗作以大胆的自我剖析、精湛的意象与强烈的情感著称，《钟形罩》与《爱丽尔》被视为女性抑郁与身份危机的真切写照，深刻影响了后来的女性写作。也有研究者指出，她的作品有时显得过度自恋，将个人痛苦戏剧化而缺乏更广阔的社会视野，她与休斯的关系及自杀也常被质疑遭到浪漫化。总体而言，她将个人痛苦转化为具有普遍共鸣的艺术，已成为美国文学经典中天才与悲剧交织的复杂文化符号。
appraisal.en: Plath is now widely recognized as a central figure of confessional poetry, celebrated for her bold self-analysis, masterful imagery, and emotional intensity; 'The Bell Jar' and 'Ariel' are read as authentic portrayals of female depression and identity crisis that profoundly shaped later women's writing. Yet some researchers argue that her work can seem overly narcissistic, dramatizing personal pain without a broader social vision, and that her marriage to Hughes and her suicide have often been romanticized. On balance, she turned personal suffering into art of universal resonance and stands as a complex cultural symbol of genius and tragedy within the American canon.

supporter.zh: 普拉斯被支持者视为女性主义文学的先驱和天才诗人。她的作品以其大胆的自我剖析、精湛的意象和情感强度而著称，为女性写作开辟了新的可能性。《钟形罩》和《爱丽尔》诗集被视为女性经历抑郁和身份危机的真实写照，激励了无数读者和作家。普拉斯通过诗歌将个人痛苦转化为艺术，展现了女性在传统社会中的挣扎与反抗，她的作品至今仍被视为女性表达内心世界的典范。
supporter.en: Plath is viewed by supporters as a pioneer of feminist literature and a poetic genius. Her works are celebrated for their bold self-analysis, masterful imagery, and emotional intensity, opening new possibilities for women's writing. 'The Bell Jar' and 'Ariel' are seen as authentic portrayals of female experiences with depression and identity crisis, inspiring countless readers and writers. Plath transformed personal pain into art through poetry, showcasing women's struggles and resistance in traditional society, and her works remain exemplars of female expression.

critic.zh: 批评者认为普拉斯的作品过度自恋，将个人痛苦戏剧化，缺乏更广阔的社会视野。一些评论家指出她的诗歌虽然技巧精湛，但内容局限于个人情感和创伤，未能超越个人经验的局限。此外，普拉斯与丈夫特德·休斯的关系也成为争议焦点，有批评者认为她在作品中将休斯妖魔化，未能客观看待婚姻中的双方责任。还有人质疑她的自杀是否被浪漫化，成为文学悲剧的象征而非真实的人性挣扎。
critic.en: Critics argue that Plath's work is overly narcissistic, dramatizing personal pain without a broader social perspective. Some commentators note that while her poetry is technically masterful, it remains confined to personal emotions and trauma, failing to transcend the limitations of individual experience. Additionally, her relationship with husband Ted Hughes has been controversial, with critics suggesting she demonized him in her work without acknowledging mutual responsibilities in their marriage. Others question whether her suicide has been romanticized, becoming a symbol of literary tragedy rather than authentic human struggle.

objective.zh: 在历史和流行文化视角下，普拉斯已成为一个复杂的文化符号，代表着天才与悲剧的结合。她的作品被纳入美国文学经典，对自白派诗歌产生了深远影响。普拉斯的生平和创作被学者们从女性主义、心理分析和文化研究等多个角度解读。在流行文化中，她的形象被不断重塑，从最初的'受苦天才'到后来被更全面地理解为一个复杂的多面人物。普拉斯的遗产在于她如何将个人痛苦转化为具有普遍共鸣的艺术，以及她如何挑战了传统对女性写作的限制。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture perspectives, Plath has become a complex cultural symbol representing the intersection of genius and tragedy. Her works are now considered part of the American literary canon, profoundly influencing confessional poetry. Her life and work have been analyzed from multiple scholarly perspectives, including feminism, psychoanalysis, and cultural studies. In popular culture, her image has been continually reinterpreted, evolving from the initial 'suffering genius' to a more nuanced understanding of her as a complex, multifaceted individual. Plath's legacy lies in how she transformed personal pain into art with universal resonance and challenged traditional limitations on women's writing.

self.zh: 我恨。我恨我的手指，我的指甲，我的头发，我的大脚趾，我的一切。我想把它们全部砍掉，然后重新开始。
self.en: I hate. I hate my fingers, my nails, my hair, my big toe, everything. I want to cut it all off and start over.
